cases.question: where are new transactions created?

required_facts.text: The transaction constructor is Transaction::new(snapshot) in src/interpreter/stm/mod.rs; it starts a Changeset at that snapshot version.

A normal owning Task creates a fresh transaction in Task::open_attempt in src/interpreter/task/mod.rs: start_txn obtains the current LiveSnapshot and the context receives TxnHandle::new(Transaction::new(live.inner.clone())).

forbidden_claims: Claim that every nested/joining task unconditionally creates an independent transaction.
Offer a constructor in a test fixture as the only production creation path.

cases.scope_note: Runtime STM world-state transactions. Require the constructor and the normal owning-task attempt entry point, not an exhaustive inventory of every constructor call or test fixture.

cases.question: show me the codepath that transaction commits take, with all the checks they go through

required_facts.text: The attempt runner calls the task/body commit_phase; it submits the changeset through retry::commit_changeset as CommitProtocol::Commit, which Committer::process sends to Committer::commit.
Before publishing, a base version ahead of the current world is rejected as FutureVersion.
A base version older than retained history is rejected as HistoryUnavailable.
Validation scans writes after the base version and rejects invalidated reads as ReadInvalidated, skipping the base version itself.
Merges are folded against committed values before any publication; a merge/type mismatch rejects the whole changeset as MergeMismatch.
Only validated changes are published. Read-only changes create no new version; writes apply a new snapshot, record write history and notify commit watchers.

evidence.needle: fn publish(&mut self, mut changeset: Changeset, transaction: bool)

required_facts.text: Physical effects are delivered only after a successful commit; conflicts lead to a new attempt with admission/backoff and an evaluation deadline rather than publishing the rejected attempt.
The commit processing path releases the disarmed base pin after validation, including rejection, and evicts history only when no live snapshots remain.

forbidden_claims: Claim that read-only transactions bypass validation.
Claim rejected attempts publish physical effects.
Claim the commit itself is cancelled merely because its reply crosses the evaluation deadline.
Invent validation of every possible write/write overlap rather than the actual read-set and merge rules.
